mission: The sabotage becomes undeniable, the countdown starts, and Torin's doorway line tells Ben the real break is now close at hand.
why_now: The timeline collapse has to be physicalised into an on-ship countdown before the chapter can move. The sabotage could not have been shown in Ch 16 without softening the Ch 16 meeting's Socratic register; delaying it to Ch 17 s1 makes the cost of the meeting specific and late. Torin's doorway line can only land now — earlier would have been premature, later would have been a surprise Ben has earned the right to see coming.
conflict: The pressure intensifies every friction. The wound's amplification is working on the group by proximity. Ben assigns tasks and tries to hear the ship sound normal. The fact that Veraine used the meeting as cover restructures Ben's understanding of the whole Ch 16 encounter retroactively — her philosophical register was sincere AND operational; both were simultaneously true. Torin steps into the frame with a sentence that is not a question.
turning_point: Torin's tone. Ben has heard the cadence before. The warmth of someone who has already decided and is negotiating the announcement. The line itself is quiet; what it announces is not.
opening_hook: The wrongness lurches. Not a jolt — a resettling, the floor of the Force dropping by another meter. Desh's sensor sweeps run backward across the last six hours and find the signature. One of the Corridor's intermediate anchor sites struck while Veraine kept them in the clearing
closing_hook: Torin's tone. Ben has heard that tone before — the certainty of someone who has already decided and is now only negotiating the announcement. The argument Torin has just announced will happen later. Ben cannot yet predict what will be in it, but he can predict its cadence
emotional_trajectory: Physical drop of the Force-floor -> retrospective understanding of the Ch 16 cover -> urgent tactical focus -> Torin's ominous calm

stakes.personal: Ben hearing the pattern in Torin's voice — the recognition crystallising without yet being named
stakes.interpersonal: Torin separating from the group emotionally even while physically present; Desh's analytical confirmation of the sabotage restructures the group's read of the meeting
stakes.external: Hours, not days, until Veraine reaches Veranthos with a compromised seal and a functioning amplification array. The race has become a sprint

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit and common area, hyperspace toward Veranthos
sensory_details: The Force settling at a new, lower floor — not a spike but a resettling, as if the ground has lowered by a meter; Desh's backward sensor sweep resolving the signature of the sabotage on a bulkhead display; Desh's countdown numeral on the bulkhead, steady against Ben's pulse; the wrongness a constant atmospheric pressure like altitude sickness sitting at the back of the head; arguments already starting to flare hotter than their content justifies in the margin of the scene; Torin's silhouette in the doorway carrying the exact weight of an old remembered cadence; the calm warmth of his voice and the edge underneath it that Ben hears and cannot yet name
canon_elements_needed: Force-wound amplification phenomenology as atmospheric/pressure metaphor
Jedi sabotage forensic procedure for Force-architecture infrastructure
action_beats: The Force-floor drops. Ben registers it in his body before his mind locates it. Desh runs the sensor sweeps backward across the meeting window and finds the sabotage signature
Desh converts the seal degradation rate to hours and posts the countdown on the cockpit display

Ben paces the common area while assigning approach tasks — nerves converting to motion; he hears his own voice coming out slightly louder than the task warrants, catches the amplification, does not explain it
Torin stands in the doorway and speaks with the calm warm tone that drops Ben's stomach — 'We need to talk about what happens when we get there.'
promises_paid: Veraine's Ch 16 meeting had operational weight beyond the philosophical register (pays Ch 16 W2 Option B promise)
notes: Keep the discovery procedural and physical. Torin's line should sound warm, calm, and fatal.
